note: Clothing and equipment (Items refill 11, job 92 design; layers M001-T11, 12 Nov 2026, master DYNASTY_MASTER_ITEMS.md s3.8 merged layer model). An item of kind clothing or gear names its body `slot` (one of `slots`) and its `wear_layer` (one of that slot's `layers`, inside to outside; a row without one takes the slot's first layer). Each slot-and-layer pair holds one piece, so a shirt goes under mail and a cloak over armour, but two cloaks, or a coat and a cloak (both body outer), are never worn at once. `spans` names more slots the piece fills at its own layer (a Dress fills body base and legs base). What a character wears is one entry per `worn` position ("slot:layer"), in that order: saved as `worn` in characters.json and sent as worn(numbers, insts) (protocol 107). The first eight positions are the eight slots of protocols 104-106 (head, body, legs, feet, hands, back, outer, waist), so an older save loads into them unchanged: each piece into its slot's base layer, and `outer` into the body's outer layer. New positions are only ever appended. Use on a clothing or gear item in the pack puts it on (ACT_WEAR; the pieces it displaces go back to the pack, and a pack without room for them refuses); the Tab screen takes each piece off (ACT_UNWEAR a = worn position). Clothing `warmth` is the 0..1 share of body heat a piece keeps, combined per slot with diminishing returns (warmth.json layer_keep) and capped by max_insulation; its `fabric` (warmth.json fabrics) sets how it behaves wet, in heat and in rain. Worn pieces stay on through death. Carrying (catalog Phase 5, master s3.9, protocol 109): one pack on the back (back:base) with a Bedroll strapped outside it (back:roll), one shoulder bag (shoulder:base), a bandolier on the chest strap (strap:base), and the belt (waist:base) with its attachment points (`belt_hangs`, at most `belt_points` used): a pouch, a quiver, a scabbard and a tool roll each have their own point. `attach` names the position a piece hangs on and what is said without it (a quiver needs no belt; on a belt it takes a point). A hotbar key whose item is not in the pack but in a `quick` bag (pouch, bandolier, scabbard) draws one into the pack and hand (master s3.9 rule 5). A worn piece's `worn_speed_mult` slows every gait (the pack frame); a worn bag's `loaded_effort` makes its load work to move with (rucksack, pack frame). A piece something hangs on cannot come off first. A bag (items.json `bag_slots`, its own slots; `bag_takes`, what goes in, rules in `bags`) holds its contents in its instance data: they stay with it worn, carried, dropped, stored or handed on, and their weight counts in full; a bag never holds a bag.

waist:pouch: A pouch hangs on a belt. Put a belt on first.
waist:scabbard: A scabbard hangs on a belt. Put a belt on first.
waist:tools: A tool roll hangs on a belt. Put a belt on first.
back:roll: A bedroll straps to the outside of a pack. Put a pack on first.

bags.note: What a bag takes (items.json bag_takes; src/shared/bag_rules.gd): small = each at most small_kg (coins, herbs, potions), small_tool = a tool of at most small_tool_kg, consumable = consumable_kinds of at most small_kg, blade = a weapon of blade_classes, arrow = ammo_class arrow (a quiver holds its ammo_capacity), any = anything not too big for a pack, awkward = anything, a large log too (the pack frame). Tuning values (master s5).
